# PostgreSQL advisory lock to serialize concurrent attempts

> A PostgreSQL transaction-scoped advisory lock acquired on a deterministic settlement identifier that serializes concurrent transactions processing the same order, preventing duplicate settlement journals despite Kafka message redelivery.

_Part of [Exactly-once guarantee with UUIDv5, advisory lock, and existence check](exactly-once-settlement.md)_

When a settlement event arrives from Kafka, multiple instances of your service might receive and process the same `order.paid` message. Without coordination, they'd all try to post the settlement journal to the ledger independently, creating duplicates. [SettlementListener](settling-orders-to-shops.md) prevents this by acquiring an advisory lock on a hashed version of the `journalId` before checking and posting. The lock works in three steps. First, a deterministic `journalId` is generated using UUIDv5 of the order—the same order always produces the same ID. Then, inside a database transaction, `pg_advisory_xact_lock(hashtext(journalId))` acquires an exclusive lock on that ID's hash, blocking any other transaction trying to lock the same `journalId`. Finally, an existence check queries whether the settlement was already posted to [`LedgerEntry`](recording-money-in-ledger.md); if it exists, the method returns early and the duplicate is discarded. The lock is held only for the duration of the transaction, so it does not starve other work. PostgreSQL's advisory locks work at the database level, not the process level, so even if you run multiple instances of the service, they coordinate through the database. Together with the deterministic ID and the existence check, the advisory lock implements the [Exactly-once guarantee with UUIDv5, advisory lock, and existence check](exactly-once-settlement.md) pattern for settlements.

**Look at:** [`SettlementListener` in settlement.listener.ts](../../../../packages/backend/libs/domains/payments/infra/settlement.listener.ts#L23)

## Pieces

- Advisory lock acquisition on journalId hash: The `pg_advisory_xact_lock(hashtext(journalId))` call that acquires an exclusive lock on the hashed `journalId`, blocking concurrent attempts to settle the same order.
- Existence check: verify settlement not already posted: The `SELECT EXISTS` query that confirms the settlement was not already posted to the ledger in a prior attempt, providing the second half of the idempotency guarantee.

## What it touches

| Kind | Name | How |
|---|---|---|
| event | `order.paid` | Triggers settlement processing; each event contains order total, shops, and line items that determine how much each shop should receive. |
| database | `LedgerEntry table` | Checked for existence of the settlement `journalId` (idempotency verification); new entries written by `ledger.post()` inside the same transaction. |
| other | `PostgreSQL advisory lock` | Held during the transaction to serialize attempts across all app instances; released automatically when the transaction ends. |

## Watch out

- Advisory locks are database-level, not process-level. If you run multiple app instances, they coordinate through the database. Plan for potential lock contention if many orders settle simultaneously.
- The lock is transaction-scoped. If your transaction takes too long, it blocks other settlements. Keep the settlement logic fast—do not call slow external services while holding the lock.
- `hashtext()` is necessary because PostgreSQL advisory locks accept a `bigint`, not text. The call would fail with a type error if you passed the `journalId` string directly.
- The lock alone is not sufficient for idempotency. If you remove the existence check, duplicate settlements can still occur due to race conditions between lock release and journal insert. You need both parts.
